words.gloss: those who are like what is seen

literal: Even if they are like the outside of a crab's eye seed, the world possesses those who are black inside like its tip.
translation: Though they appear as bright red as the outside of a crab's eye seed, the world contains those whose hearts are as black as that seed's tip.
modern: வெளியே குன்றிமணியின் சிவந்த நிறத்தைப் போல நல்லவர்களாகக் தோன்றினாலும், உள்ளே அக்குன்றிமணியின் மூக்கைப் போலக் கரிய மனமுடையவர்களை இவ்வுலகம் கொண்டுள்ளது.
explanation: This couplet uses the striking image of the 'kunri' seed (crab's eye seed) to expose hypocrites who practice false asceticism. The seed is brilliantly red and beautiful on the outside, but has a distinct black spot at its tip. Similarly, some people appear pure, virtuous, and radiant on the outside, but their inner minds are filled with dark, evil thoughts. The poet warns that the world contains such deceptive individuals, urging us to look beyond outward appearances.
